findings.detail: Line 30 imports `{ existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync }` from `node:fs` — `readdirSync` is not among them, but line 91 calls it. The call is wrapped in `try { … } catch { return null; }`, and a `ReferenceError` for an undefined identifier is caught by that handler just like an I/O error. So `readAxeShards` returns `null` on every invocation, execution falls through to `readJsonOrNull('.apexyard/raw/axe.json')`, and the per-worker merge added in this PR is dead code from the first run. This regresses to precisely the failure the function's own docblock says it exists to fix: `e2e/accessibility.spec.ts` scans three pages (`the landing view`, `the QR tool`, `the Compare Files tool`, lines 150/155/161) and writes one shard per worker, but the committed `.apexyard/accessibility-report.json` records `pages_scanned: ["the Compare Files tool"]` and 8 violation nodes — one worker's subset, with `passed: false` computed against the 7-node budget on incomplete data. The evidence bundle is the artifact CI verifies and a human reads, so a silently truncated accessibility section is a wrong answer presented with the same confidence as a right one. No test exercises this path: `scripts/tests/test-evidence.sh` never creates `test-results/axe-summary.*.json` (its fixture dir does not exist, so `existsSync` short-circuits before the missing identifier is ever reached), and `tests/unit/evidence.test.ts` only tests `collectAccessibility` on a hand-built object.
findings.summary: readAxeShards uses readdirSync without importing it; the bare catch hides it

findings.detail: The line reads `run_stage "11. Evidence self-check" \n    node scripts/verify-evidence.mjs …` — a literal backslash-n where a line continuation was intended (compare the correctly-written `\` + newline form in the `else` branch at lines 241-243). Outside quotes bash resolves `\n` to the word `n`, so `run_stage` shifts off the label and runs `n node scripts/verify-evidence.mjs --base … --require-gate high`. There is no command `n`, so the stage records `FAIL(127)`, sets `FAILED=1`, and the script prints `Local gates failed. Do not push.` and exits 1 — which `.githooks/pre-push:81` turns into `push aborted`. This fires on the `ALREADY_ATTESTED=1` branch, i.e. the ordinary case of re-pushing content whose review is already on disk (the branch the surrounding comment was written to make cheap). The failure is also maximally misleading: the summary blames the evidence self-check, whose real command never ran, and the documented escape hatch is `git push --no-verify` — which is exactly how a gate stops guarding anything.
findings.summary: Literal `\n` makes the pre-push gate fail spuriously on the already-attested path

findings.detail: `files_with_findings: json.filter(…).map((f) => toPosixRelative(f.filePath, root)).sort().length` computes relative paths for every ESLint file with findings, sorts them, then keeps only the count. The `.map()` and `.sort()` results are thrown away, so the work is pure waste and — more to the point — the shape reads like an editing casualty: the mapping to POSIX-relative paths and the sort only make sense if the *list* was meant to be emitted (that is exactly why a deterministic sort would be needed). As written, `root` is threaded into `collectEslint` for no observable effect. Harmless at this scale, but the next reader has to decide whether the list was dropped deliberately or by accident.
findings.summary: files_with_findings maps and sorts an array only to discard it and take .length

findings.detail: `export { readJson, existsSync, statSync };` re-exports two `node:fs` functions and one private helper. Nothing imports them: `scripts/evidence.mjs:36-40` imports only the `collect*` functions and `SEVERITY_ORDER`, and `tests/unit/evidence.test.ts` imports neither (no occurrence of `readJson`, `existsSync`, or `statSync` in the suite). `readJson` (line 24) is itself unreferenced inside this module — the collectors all take already-parsed JSON — and `statSync` appears only in the line 16 import and this re-export, so it exists solely to be re-exported. Re-exporting `node:fs` from a domain module also blurs the boundary: a future caller could reach `fs` through `collectors.mjs` rather than importing it directly.
findings.summary: Dead export: readJson, existsSync, and statSync have no consumer

findings.detail: Lines 102-109 add a careful explanation that this file is deliberately *not* excluded from its own sweep, including the verification that none of the patterns match their own literal text (every prefix is followed by `[`, which is outside each character class). Two leftover comments from the previous behaviour survive and say the opposite: lines 128-129 (`Skipping this file is not cosmetic: it necessarily contains every pattern it searches for, so including it guarantees a self-match`) and line 153 (`Skipping the pattern-list lines themselves, now that the file is in scope`). Neither describes any code — `list_scan_targets` has no exclusion and the loop has no filter. In a security script this is worse than ordinary comment rot: the surviving comment asserts a self-match is guaranteed, which is a standing invitation for the next maintainer to re-add the exclusion and reintroduce the blind spot lines 102-109 were written to close.
findings.summary: Stale comments claim the scanner skips itself, contradicting the code and the comment above

findings.detail: The comment added at lines 19-21 states `No baseUrl: it is deprecated in TS 6 and removed in 7` and explains that `paths` resolves relative to the config file when baseUrl is absent — but line 18 sets `"baseUrl": "."`, and the pre-existing TD-001 comment immediately above it explains why that setting is needed. Two adjacent comments now contradict each other and one contradicts the config. Whoever reads this next either removes a `baseUrl` the TD-001 note says is load-bearing, or spends time working out which comment is stale. Zero runtime impact today — `baseUrl: "."` and an absent baseUrl resolve `./node_modules/@e965/xlsx` identically from the repo root.
findings.summary: New comment says "No baseUrl" directly below `"baseUrl": "."`

findings.detail: `if (e.name.startsWith('.') && e.name !== '.githooks') continue;` carves out `.githooks` from the dotfile skip, but the only files `walkSources` collects are those whose extension is in `SOURCE_EXT` (`.ts` / `.tsx`, line 357). `.githooks/pre-push` — the sole entry, added in this PR — has no extension, so descending into the directory yields nothing and the exception has no effect on `architecture.json`. Not a defect; flagging it because the special case reads as intentional coverage of the hooks directory, and a later reader may assume hooks are counted in the architecture snapshot when they are not.
findings.summary: The `.githooks` exception in walkSources can never match anything
